paper_title: Stellar cooling bounds on new light particles: plasma mixing effects
notes: This is a theoretical paper deriving improved stellar cooling bounds on dark photons, B-L vectors, and generic scalars by including plasma mixing effects. While it derives new theoretical bounds (up to 3 orders of magnitude improvement for light scalars), these are not based on new experimental measurements or direct observational data. The bounds depend critically on uncertain supernova models and are described by the authors as 'order-of-magnitude estimates at best'. The paper improves calculations of existing stellar cooling constraints (known from SN1987A observations and stellar models) rather than reporting new observational exclusions. The main results are: (1) improved bounds on light scalars coupling to electrons/nucleons, (2) revised dark photon bounds from SN1987A, (3) B-L vector bounds, (4) Higgs portal scalar constraint sin θ ≲ 3×10^-10 for m ≲ 2 keV. None of the primary results (scalar couplings α_φee, α_φNN) match the canonical coupling conventions exactly. This paper is best characterized as providing improved theoretical estimates for known constraint mechanisms rather than new experimental limits.
